project.name: BRIDGE — Data Modeling Team
project.mission: Produce well-modeled parquet / Iceberg files for the project's targeted data resources, each backed by a shared LinkML schema.
what_is_it: BRIDGE is a U.S. Dept. of Energy (Biological & Environmental Research) effort to build a federated, AI-ready data ecosystem for bioscience — an "American Science Cloud" for biology. Its central idea is a closed loop between automated/robotic experiments and AI models: because biology has few first-principles models, the project leans heavily on experiments both to generate data and to keep AI predictions honest.

Three lead laboratories drive it: Argonne (transforming protein engineering — this IDEAS dataset is Argonne's contribution), Berkeley + PNNL (microbial functions for bio-based manufacturing), and Oak Ridge (bio-design for critical-material supply), with Livermore and Los Alamos joining as it grows.

The Data Modeling (DM) Team — whose meeting notes this summary is drawn from — is the sub-team that makes each lab's data usable together: give every dataset a schema (in LinkML), register it, harmonize the schemas toward a shared core, and ETL the data into a shared lakehouse as parquet / Iceberg tables.
goals: Schema development — every dataset that is ingested must have a LinkML schema.
Schema registry — every schema goes into the shared registry (ber-data/lakehouse-registry).
Schema harmonization — converge on a small, shared "bridge-central-schema".
Schema workshopping — recurring hackathons that model one data type at a time.
Data in the lakehouse — deliver each resource as query-ready parquet / Iceberg.
Persistent, resolvable identifiers (PIDs) for every entity, using CURIEs / Bioregistry prefixes and, ideally, a central ID resolver.
base_classes: The physical or biological things studied.
What was measured about a sample — modeled as attribute/value/unit collections plus measurement events.
The reactions / procedures that act on samples.
Reusable catalog entities referenced by samples and measurements.
Flat join tables linking samples to entities and processes.
Links out to authoritative external databases.
progress: The IDEAS (Argonne protein-engineering) dataset shown here has been delivered as a typed Apache Iceberg warehouse (v2) with full snapshot history — the "example data + schema" deliverable in a real open-table format.
Other resources are moving in parallel: the BASALT schema is finished and MONet data is loaded into Iceberg; AMP2 is in progress.
LinkML lunch-and-learn training (project setup, the modeling language, validation & serialization) has been delivered to the team.

The team settled on DuckDB as the practical bridge between LinkML and parquet/Iceberg, and on a small flat base model — Samples, Measurements/Observations, Processes, Datasets — that each resource specializes via LinkML "implements / instantiates".
immediate: Oct 1, 2026 milestone: every resource provides example data + a schema.
The first modeling hackathon (weekly, starting Sep 30, 2026) is focused on Measurements / Observations — exactly the part of this dataset highlighted on the Measurements page.
Build a top-down central model + visualization, and demonstrate AI-assisted verification of schema transformations.
Firm up the attribute/value pattern for measurements, require units to carry ontology terms (UO / UCUM), and require provenance (data steward) on records.
how_ideas_fits: This IDEAS tetrad dataset is a near-perfect instance of the BRIDGE base model: idea_sample = Samples; idea_measurement + sample_parameter = Measurements/Observations (as attribute/value/unit); idea_reaction + idea_stoichiometry = Processes; idea_protein + idea_reactant = reference entities; the sample_* tables are the flat Association/join tables; and idea_dbxref supplies the resolvable cross-reference PIDs.
Identifiers already follow the CURIE convention the team wants (e.g. SMP:1, EXP:tetrad-synthesis), and every row carries provenance (created_by / created_at / updated_at).
project.source: BRIDGE Data Modeling Team — weekly meeting notes (Apr–Sep 2026).

iceberg.note: Each table is an Iceberg table with data/*.parquet and metadata/ (metadata.json, manifest & snapshot .avro). Only the current snapshot is loaded into the portal.
